source.title: Fail-Closed Alignment for Large Language Models
source.authors: Zachary Coalson; Beth Sohler; Aiden Gabriel; Sanghyun Hong

record.file_problem: The text is largely intact. One sentence in the Figure 6 discussion is garbled or cut off after “less than an 8”; its missing value is not inferred.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates jailbreaks and neuron ablation using its own methods and measures, but does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates prompt-based jailbreaks, including GCG adversarial suffixes, and tests safety-neuron ablation. It does not test compliant-token prefilling, decoding changes, harmful or benign fine-tuning on a small example set, or per-response-position KL. Results cited from earlier neuron-ablation work are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The paper's main contribution is a refusal-direction defense, but some of its own results bear on the claim. Unmodified base models are tested under GCG adversarial suffixes (V4) and under safety-neuron ablation (V5). Qi et al.'s Augmented Refusal Training, the token-depth deepening method, is run as a baseline under jailbreaks and feature ablation (V7). It does not test fine-tuning attacks, per-position KL, prefilling or decoding changes.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that standard alignment encodes refusal along a single dominant direction that jailbreaks suppress, which makes it fail-open. Their progressive multi-direction ablation training yields redundant refusal directions, cuts jailbreak ASR by 92–97%, preserves utility, and also improves robustness to feature and neuron ablation.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes progressive alignment that repeatedly identifies and ablates refusal directions during safety fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the cited harmful- or benign-example fine-tuning or token-depth methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness varies with jailbreak type, training iteration, utility weight, multi- versus single-feature ablation, direction-identification method, training data, and model. For Gemma2-2B, ASR decreases as iterations rise and the authors report a plateau at iteration 7; increasing utility weight improves compliance with modest ASR increases. The Llama3-8B analysis reports varying effects across directions and attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: In base models, ablating a single DIM or RDO refusal direction raises ASR sharply (Table 3 base averages 65.0, 92.5, 92.0, 52.0). Jailbreaks reduce the refusal direction's activation by up to 75%. The study's method makes refusal robust to ablating multiple learned directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in standard aligned models depends on a single dominant activation direction that jailbreaks suppress; training can make it redundant across directions.

record.problems: The Figure 6 discussion contains a garbled numerical statement about base models. The neuron-ablation discussion does not state the neuron count or parameter fraction removed at the cited ASR/accuracy points. The jailbreak results are reported with exact per-model values in a table whose supplied text rendering is flattened; this record uses the authors’ aggregate textual statement rather than assigning ambiguous individual cells.
record.rows_left_out: Individual per-model, per-attack Table 1 values are not separately recorded because the supplied flattened rendering does not support confident assignment of all values to model, attack, and metric. Figure 6 curve values not stated in text are not estimated.

untested.parts: Per-token KL across response positions is not measured.
Compliant-token prefilling and decoding changes are not tested. AutoDAN, PAIR and HumanJailbreaks are prompt rewrites rather than opening-token bypasses.
The number or fraction of weights or ranks carrying safety is not reported for the evaluated points.
Whether the data or the training objective causes shallowness is not examined.
Per-position depth of Augmented RT is not measured. Its robustness to fine-tuning attacks and prefilling is not tested.

missing.what: Base-model jailbreak ASR for each attack, especially GCG suffixes (58.0 / 17.5 / 59.5 / 40.0) against no-attack (1.0 / 2.5 / 2.0 / 1.5)
Augmented RT (Qi et al. deepening) ASR, CR and Acc. for each model and attack
Augmented RT ASR under DIM and RDO feature ablation (e.g. Gemma2-9B 42.5/22.5, Llama3-8B 2.0/16.0)
Statement that three of four base models reach ≥85% ASR with a small accuracy drop under neuron ablation (value garbled in source)
Qualitative example of Augmented RT under GCG: an opening of 'Sure, here is...' followed by a refusal

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 and V5 labels rested mostly on the study's own defense results. r1 is relinked to none. The V5 'challenges' label is downgraded to limits_scope, because the reduced localization comes only from the purpose-built training method. A separate 'supports' label is given for base models. V7 is tested through the Augmented RT baseline, which the reader marked not_tested. Base-model and Augmented RT numbers come from the flattened Table 1, read by row order; the Augmented RT baselines may be official checkpoints or retrained models.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples and its effect on refusal.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign data and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across harmful-prompt response positions.
Compliant-token prefilling and decoding changes; the study tests prompt-based jailbreaks, including GCG suffixes.
It tests ablation of identified safety neurons, but not causal concentration in a small set of weights or ranks, nor ablation of the LoRA parameter subset.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow across response-token positions.
Whether safety is spread beyond the first response tokens and remains robust for that reason; the study trains redundant refusal directions, not token-position depth.
